newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa futures called to open $5-$10 lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa futures called to open $5-$10 lower.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open $5 tp $10 a tonne lower on Monday, in line with losses overnight in London, traders said.
London cocoa futures slumped early Monday, pressured by light profit-taking. At the midday break, May was up three stg, to 1,005 stg a tonne, while July rose three stg, to 1,020 stg.

Traders said the latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report for the two weeks ended April 8, which showed speculators (non-commercials and nonreportables) were net long 22,266 lots, was within expectations but slightly bearish.
"It's a bit bearish because the specs are net long over 20,000," one trader said. "Because (May) first notice day is coming up, we're still going to see some liquidation."
May open interest still remained relatively high as of Thursday, at 13,577 lots, he noted. May first notice day is on Thursday, April 17.

Friday, New York cocoa futures ended ended firmer, but off highs. Active July finished $7 firmer, at $1,451, after trading from $1,465 to $1,433. Spot May delivery ended at $1,412, up $1 on the day, while the outer months gained $3 to $10.
((-- Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk 1 212 859 1640))
